phenotypes: above average or macrocephalic head circumference
intellectual disability (milder than other HJS types)
Could be inherited from non-symptomatic parent, suggesting dominant-negative mechanism

clinical.citation: A recurrent variant in PPP2R5C identified in individuals with macrocephaly, intellectual disability, and seizures (PMID: 39696819)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Recurrent de novo variant in unrelated individuals, Glu153 is part of highly conserved acidic loop that directly interacts with PP2A catalytic subunit

biological.citation: Pathogenic de novo variants in PPP2R5C cause a neurodevelopmental disorder within the Houge-Janssens syndrome spectrum (PMID: 39978342)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C encodes the regulatory B56γ subunit of PP2A. De novo missense variants in PPP2R5C cause neurodevelopmental disorder with features including developmental delay, hypotonia, epilepsy, and macrocephaly. Variants affect substrate binding, C-subunit binding, or both, with variable effects on catalytic activity. Loss-of-function variants can be inherited from asymptomatic parents, suggesting dominant-negative mechanism.

biological.citation: LincR-PPP2R5C Promotes Th2 Cell Differentiation Through PPP2R5C/PP2A by Forming an RNA-DNA Triplex in Allergic Asthma (PMID: 38262392)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C is a regulatory subunit of PP2A that regulates Th2 cell differentiation in asthma. A long noncoding RNA (LincR-PPP2R5C) forms an RNA-DNA triplex with the PPP2R5C promoter to enhance PPP2R5C expression and activate PP2A phosphatase activity, promoting Th2 polarization and airway inflammation.
biological.sample_size: Mouse model of ovalbumin-induced acute asthma

biological.citation: Structural feature and biological function of PPP2R5C gene (PMID: 19840435)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C is a regulatory subunit of PP2A that plays critical roles in cell proliferation, differentiation, and transformation through dephosphorylation of p53 at various residues. Altered expression patterns of PPP2R5C are associated with malignant cell transformation and serve as a marker for progressive disease in B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

biological.citation: Expression and distribution of PPP2R5C gene in leukemia (PMID: 21548944)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C expression is significantly elevated in AML, CML, T-ALL, and B-CLL compared to healthy controls. Five transcript variants of PPP2R5C are identified with similar frequencies across leukemia types and healthy samples. Overexpression of PPP2R5C in T-cell and myeloid malignancies correlates with cell proliferation and differentiation.
biological.sample_size: 77 de novo leukemia patients, 26 CR patients, 20 healthy controls
biological.significance: p<0.05 for elevated expression in AML, CML, T-ALL, B-CLL vs controls

biological.citation: LincR-PPP2R5C regulates IL-1β ubiquitination in macrophages and promotes airway inflammation and emphysema in a murine model of COPD (PMID: 39018689)
biological.summary: LincR-PPP2R5C regulates IL-1β ubiquitination in macrophages through PP2A activity. LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency increases ubiquitinated IL-1β levels and reduces IL-1β protein expression, ameliorating emphysema and pulmonary inflammation in COPD models. PP2A activity modulates IL-1β post-translational modification.

biological.citation: The Relationship between PPP2R5C and Molt-4 Cell Viability, HSP90-GR Signal in Childhood Acute T Lymphocytic Leukemia (PMID: 35123608)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C knockdown via siRNA in Molt-4 T-ALL cells significantly reduces cell proliferation, blocks cells in G2 phase, and increases apoptosis. PPP2R5C downregulation inhibits HSP90-GR signaling pathway, suggesting this pathway mediates PPP2R5C effects on leukemic cell viability.
biological.significance: p<0.05 for proliferation, EdU incorporation, apoptosis, and cell cycle changes

biological.citation: Combined detection of SDC2/ADHFE1/PPP2R5C methylation in stool DNA for colorectal cancer screening (PMID: 37270460)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C gene methylation levels are significantly increased in colorectal cancer patient stool samples. Combined detection of SDC2/ADHFE1/PPP2R5C methylation achieves 84.8% sensitivity and 98.0% specificity for CRC detection with AUC of 0.930, suggesting PPP2R5C methylation as a biomarker for CRC screening.
biological.sample_size: 105 CRC, 54 advanced adenoma, 57 non-advanced adenoma, 47 polyps, 100 NED controls

biological.citation: An Exploration of Osteosarcoma Metastasis Diagnostic Markers Based on Tumor-Associated Neutrophils (PMID: 37272097)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C is identified as a potential marker for osteosarcoma metastasis through weighted gene co-expression network analysis of tumor-associated neutrophils. PPP2R5C knockdown reduces OS cell proliferation and migration while increasing apoptosis via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, affecting p-AKT protein levels.
biological.sample_size: U2-OS and MG63 osteosarcoma cell lines
biological.significance: p<0.01 for expression, proliferation, migration, apoptosis, and p-AKT changes

biological.citation: Differential gene expression profiles of PPP2R5C-siRNA-treated malignant T cells (PMID: 23941244)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C knockdown via siRNA in Molt-4 and Jurkat T cells significantly reduces proliferation without inducing apoptosis. Global gene expression profiling reveals 439 upregulated and 524 downregulated genes, with changes in TCR, Wnt, calcium, MAPK, and p53 signaling pathways. GSK-3β, ATM, and MDM2 genes play important roles in PPP2R5C knockdown effects.
biological.sample_size: Molt-4 and Jurkat T cell lines
biological.significance: p<0.05 for proliferation reduction at 72h; twofold gene expression changes

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - Characterization of de novo variants in PPP2R5C expands the spectrum of PP2A-related neurodevelopmental disorders (E. Brimble et al.)
biological.summary: De novo missense variants in PPP2R5C impair binding of PP2A catalytic C and structural A subunits and reduce PP2A catalytic activity. The recurrent p.E122K variant, affecting a residue that directly interacts with the catalytic subunit, shows significantly impaired subunit binding and phosphatase activity compared to wildtype.

biological.citation: ASHG 2015 - Molecular Markers of Blood Pressure Response to Thiazide Diuretics Identified Through Whole Transcriptome RNA-Seq Analysis (A. Costa Sa et al.)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C is identified as differentially expressed in relation to chlorthalidone blood pressure response. The SNP rs1203488 in PPP2R5C is associated with chlorthalidone BP response in whites, with variant allele carriers showing reduced BP response.
biological.sample_size: 50 whites from PEAR; 50 whites and 50 blacks from PEAR-2
